sections.html:
Miramar sits at the southwest edge of Broward County. The Broward County Property Appraiser assesses your house, and the city tacks its own fees onto the same bill. Population is 137,107 across 31 square miles, bounded roughly by Pembroke Road to the north, County Line Road or Honey Hill Road to the south, U.S. Highway 441 (State Road 7) to the east and the Everglades Conservation Area to the west.

The city was incorporated on May 26, 1955, and grew from under 200 residents on about 2.9 square miles. That is why a house from the 1960s and a much newer one can stand a few miles apart and come with very different permit files, association rules and flood exposure. Start with your own permit and lien history instead of a citywide average.

sections.h2: What Miramar puts on a property tax bill
sections.html:
Broward's appraiser sets the assessed value, several taxing authorities set rates, and bills go out each year starting November 1. Of every ad valorem tax dollar, 35 cents goes to the city and 65 cents to other Broward taxing agencies.

Miramar charges on the tax bill
ChargeAmount
City millageProposed to stay at 7.1172 (no change)
Fire assessment, residential unit$479.21 per year
Fire assessment, mobile home$221.44 per year
Stormwater fee$120 per equivalent residential unit
One equivalent residential unit3,619 square feet

Call the Broward tax office or the city for the millage rate that applies to your closing year. The fire and stormwater charges are non-ad valorem assessments. They show up on the same bill but do not rise or fall with your home's value. The city also runs a fire fee hardship exemption for qualified homeowners, with an application window each year.

Building permit applications go through an online portal that stays open around the clock, with counter help on limited weekdays. A residential permit usually takes about 15 business days to issue, and building fees carry an 8 percent surcharge. For questions before a home improvement project, call the Building Division at 954-602-3200.

Records matter at closing. The city is not likely to hold blueprints for homes more than 10 years past their certificate of occupancy, because state rules let it discard residential plans after that. If you did work years ago, look up the permit now so a buyer's inspector does not find an open or expired one.

  • An electric vehicle charger at home needs a city permit and inspection, even under a utility install program.
  • Homes in an association also need association approval for a charger.
  • Only people listed as contacts on a code case can check its status online.

The city offers a lien search, and a check for it must match the exact fee. Order one early so no lien appears for the first time on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: Deed tax, homestead and delinquent taxes
sections.html:
A Broward deed carries the base statewide stamp rate of 70 cents for each $100 of consideration, paid to the county clerk at recording. Everyone on the deed is liable, so the contract should name who pays.

  • Homestead applications reach the property appraiser by March 1. The Broward office takes exemption questions at 954-357-6830.
  • The TRIM notice arrives in August, and a value petition is due with the clerk within 25 days.
  • The early payment discount slides from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February.
  • Unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1, and tax certificates are sold by June 1.

A sale resets a homesteaded property's assessment to just value on the next January 1, so the buyer's first bill can differ sharply from yours. A certificate holder cannot demand payment until two years after April 1 of the year of issuance, but a tax deed application can follow. Clear any delinquent taxes before you list.

sections.h2: How can I sell a Miramar house fast?
sections.html:
Sellers here usually compare a listing, a direct sale and a cash bid. Condition, loan payoff and your deadline drive the choice. A cash offer typically saves weeks but comes in below a retail price, so collect more than one written number.

  • Listing: widest buyer pool, with repair requests after inspection.
  • Direct sale to an investor: as-is purchase and a closing date you can bend.
  • Short sale or pre-foreclosure sale: needs lender approval and starts before a judgment.

If a lender has already sued, Florida rules put the auction 20 to 35 days after final judgment, require a 5 percent bidder deposit and allow a 10 day objection window. Selling ahead of that date keeps the price in your hands.

sections.h2: What to gather before accepting an offer
sections.html:
Pull together the items that set your net proceeds before you sign. Miramar has several charges outside the base tax rate.

  • The fire assessment and stormwater lines from your tax bill. The residential fire assessment is $479.21 a year, and stormwater is $120 per equivalent residential unit of 3,619 square feet.
  • Proof of your homestead or other exemption from the Broward County Property Appraiser.
  • A city lien search and a list of permits pulled on the property.
  • Association documents and any balance owed, if the home is in a community with dues.

The fire assessment helps maintain fire ratings that can lower insurance costs, and a buyer's agent may bring that up. Have your insurance declaration page on hand before you negotiate.

sections.h2: Steps from signed contract to closing
sections.html:
After a contract is signed, the title company searches the record for liens, open permits and tax balances. You order payoff letters from each lender, and the association issues its paperwork if the home has one. Resolve anything the search turns up, because a lien from the city or a permit left open will surface for the buyer's lender. At the signing, the deed is executed and sent to the county clerk, who collects the stamp tax and records it.

A cash buyer can skip the appraisal and loan underwriting, so most of the remaining time goes to the title search and payoffs.

faqs.q: Who sets the property tax rate for a Miramar house?
faqs.a: Several taxing authorities do, while the Broward County Property Appraiser sets the assessed value. The city has proposed a millage of 7.1172, so confirm the final figure with the city or the Broward tax collector.

faqs.q: How long does a Miramar building permit take?
faqs.a: About 15 business days for a residential project. Plan for that if a buyer wants an old issue closed out before the sale.

faqs.q: Will a buyer ask for permit records on my Miramar home?
faqs.a: Often a buyer's inspector will ask about permits on past work. The city is not likely to keep plans for homes more than 10 years past the certificate of occupancy, so search for yours early.

faqs.q: What is the Miramar fire assessment?
faqs.a: It is a yearly non-ad valorem fee on the property tax bill that pays for fire and emergency resources. A residential unit pays $479.21 per year, and qualified homeowners can apply for a hardship exemption.

faqs.q: Where can I check for liens before selling in Miramar?
faqs.a: Use the city's lien search through its Financial Services pages and ask your title company for a full title search. Pay for the lien search in the exact amount required.
